title: SLA-aware GPU memory reserve planner for weights, KV shards, and activations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: produce an SLA-aware GPU memory budgeting plan that explicitly divides per-GPU reserved capacity across model weights, KV cache shards, and activation working set, with measurable safety margins ('reserve' aka 'safety buffer') to avoid OOMs under tail-load bursts and prioritized latency SLOs. This ticket produces the modeling, a small synthetic and live benchmark matrix, and an ops-ready config templating approach so Dedicated and Private deployments can apply conservative defaults and optionally tighten for cost.
proposed_strategy: 1) Baseline footprint estimation: for target model families (e.g., RWKV/GPT-style LLMs at 7B/13B/30B), capture three components per model: weights (quantized footprint), static KV shard overhead, and per-request activation working set (sequence-dependent).

2) Quantized weight allocation: assume production default quantization Q4_0 for weights unless flagged. Record both compressed on-disk size and decompressed inference memory (kernel temporary overhead). Example target: 7B -> weights 6.0 GB (q4), 13B -> 11.0 GB (q4).

3) KV cache sharding model: model KV is sharded across GPUs for multi-GPU placements and sharded-per-socket for single-GPU. Use formula KV_bytes = tokens_cached * hidden_size * 2 (float16) * head_count_adjustment. Recommend a conservative KV reservation of 1.15x observed steady-state to cover jitter and in-flight writes.

4) Activation working set: model attention and intermediate activations scale with beam/seq-length and batch. Model per-request activation estimate uses A = base_activation_per_token * max_seq_length * effective_batch. For burst safety use peak_batch = observed_p50*2 or configured burst limit, whichever larger.

5) Safety margin & reserve policy: two-tier reserve: critical_reserve (for SLA-protection) = max(8% of total GPU memory, 0.5 GB), op_reserve (for opportunistic headroom to absorb KV insert bursts) = 1.1x KV + 1.05x activation baseline. Critical_reserve must not be sacrificed by autoscaling decisions without explicit override.

6) Allocation order on GPU: immutable weights pinned first -> critical_reserve pinned second -> KV shards allocation -> activations buffer (dynamically grown with preemption signals to batching controller).

7) Runtime knobs to implement: per-model memory profile metadata, 'reserve_mode' (strict|optimistic), kv_reserved_ratio (default 0.15), activation_slack_pct (default 5%), and 'oom_preempt_threshold' to trigger graceful shedding/fallbacks.

8) Cost/control trade-off guidance: tighter reserves reduce idle headroom and improve utilization but increase OOM risk for tail bursts. Provide recommended presets: 'conservative' (default for enterprise), 'balanced' (for Dedicated with SLA 99.9%), 'aggressive' (for non-critical dev workloads).
experiment_plan: A) Synthetic sweep: for each model size (7B/13B/30B) run matrix of batch sizes {1,2,4,8} and seq-lens {128,512,1024} to measure: peak GPU allocation, transient spikes, KV growth rate per second, and time-to-reclaim after request finishes.
B) Live traffic shadowing: route 5% of production traffic as shadow to a dedicated cluster with current 'conservative' reserve and record OOM events and latency tail (p95/p99/p999).
C) Fault-injection: artificially delay KV deallocation in the runtime to simulate slower GC and observe how much reserve is needed to avoid cascading OOMs.

D) Metrics to capture: 'gpu_mem_total', 'gpu_mem_free', 'weights_committed', 'kv_committed', 'activations_committed', 'oom_count', 'preemptions_triggered', and trace annotated with request_id and seq_len. Store benchmark traces in the perf-dashboard and attach links to results.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement metadata + reserve knobs in runtime (PR # to follow). Ship behind feature flag 'reserve-planner-v1'.
2) Canary: enable for a small Dedicated cluster (non-prod) with conservative preset. Run Synth sweep + 24h shadowing. Verify no OOM regressions and stable latency.
3) Gradual ramp: enable 'balanced' preset for selected tenants with alerting on any OOM or preemption. Iterate on ratios based on observed KV growth delta.
4) Docs: add 'GPU memory budgeting' page to Console docs and add default presets for Dedicated and Private install manifests.
5) Ops playbook: add runbook steps for when 'gpu_mem_free' falls below critical_reserve: scale policy, enable eviction, or fallback model variant.
acceptance_criteria: A) Models 7B/13B/30B run all synthetic matrix without binary OOMs on target presets (conservative/balanced).
B) Shadowing shows <=1 OOM per 100k requests and latency tail increase <5% relative to baseline.
C) Dashboard widgets created with live breakdown by weights/KV/activations and automated alerts when free memory < critical_reserve.
D) Runtime exposes metadata and reserve knobs usable by Console for policy configuration.
